clue.text: Founder of college, eg becoming an afterthought

indicators.note: one part of the word turns into something else, so the letters spelling eg give way to a replacement

parts.note: the word is used in full and then altered
the letters E and G inside the word
A plus PS, the postscript added as an afterthought to a letter

explanation.surface: Someone who started a college finds they are now only an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Founder' looks like a noun for the college's creator; it is the verb meaning to fall in. In COLLEGE the EG is replaced by A PS.
explanation.definitionFit: To founder is to give way or fail, as a building or a plan caves in.

clue.text: America's party — no intellectual there?

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
of America read as 'of US'

explanation.surface: A jibe that a big American political party has no thinkers in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America's party' reads as DO OF US, a party belonging to the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A doofus is American slang for a stupid person, the opposite of a thinker.

clue.text: Not normally fusty — and fun?

indicators.note: letters set out other than in their normal order are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that is fresh rather than musty might well be enjoyable.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of FUSTY and FUN are rearranged, and the whole clue also describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstuffy means informal and relaxed, the opposite of old-fashioned and fusty.

clue.text: Paper parrot?

definitions.meaning: the Daily ..., a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper, and to mirror is to copy as a parrot copies words.

clue.text: Keeping mum, sidekick's outside in disguise

parts.note: stocking means keeping goods in store
ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: only the outer letters of the word are used, its first and last

explanation.surface: A loyal assistant stays silent while going about in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping mum' looks like one phrase for staying silent, but it splits in two. 'outside' takes S and K, the first and last letters of sidekick.
explanation.definitionFit: A nylon stocking pulled over the face is a robber's classic disguise.

clue.text: Perfect, keeping most of cipher in foreign language

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a cipher is an old word for zero, nought

explanation.surface: A flawless rendering of a code into another tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Azeri is the Turkic language spoken in Azerbaijan.

clue.text: Drew, painted, etc, art, taking turns to exhibit

indicators.note: the run of letters is turned round to read in the opposite direction
the words display a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: Someone drew and painted, trying various kinds of art in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to exhibit' shows DETCARTTA running through 'painted, etc, art, taking'; 'turns' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Drew in the sense of pulled in or lured, as a crowd is drawn to a show.

clue.text: One in unemployment black spot protected by card

indicators.note: the second piece sits inside the first for protection

parts.note: the joker is a playing card
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to spot something is to see it

explanation.surface: An unlucky black mark is shielded by a playing card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black spot' looks like one thing, an unlucky place or the pirate's token, but splits into B and SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A jobseeker is a person out of work and looking for employment.

clue.text: American done with loom, finally leaving this?

definitions.text: American done with loom, finally leaving this?

parts.note: thru is the American spelling of through, meaning finished

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Asks what a weaver leaves behind once finished at the loom.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the threads left on the loom when the cloth is cut away.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrum is the fringe of warp threads left on a loom after the woven cloth is cut off.

clue.text: Recondition derelict motorway emergency centre?

indicators.note: something derelict is broken down, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is used for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Instructions to renovate an abandoned motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident room is a police headquarters set up to run a major investigation or emergency.

clue.text: Enemy within a month or two's heading back to the front

indicators.note: the turned letters go before the other piece
the short run of letters is reversed
the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: Jan is the abbreviation for January

explanation.surface: Within a month or two, someone returns to the battle front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns OR plus T (the first letter of two) into TRO, and 'to the front' puts that ahead of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trojan horse is a subversive agent working from the inside, an enemy within.

clue.text: Catch to fumble?

definitions.meaning: to struggle clumsily or be in difficulties

explanation.definitionFit: A flounder is a flatfish an angler may catch, and to flounder is to struggle or blunder.

clue.text: Wrong righted, ignoring tip from flag waver

indicators.note: the letters are put wrong, that is rearranged
a letter is left out of the word
the end letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A mistake corrected, overlooking someone waving a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag waver' looks like one phrase; 'flag' gives G, its tip, and 'waver' is the definition. RIGHTED less G is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to be indecisive, to hesitate or waver.

clue.text: Request PCs, perhaps, causing court problems?

parts.note: to request is to ask for
personal computers are an example of IT, information technology

explanation.surface: Asking for computers could cause legal trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court but is the verb, to invite.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask for it is to invite trouble, as by provoking punishment.

clue.text: Peacenik in front of judge rising

parts.note: CO stands for conscientious objector
up before a judge, appearing in court

explanation.surface: A pacifist stands up before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' looks like part of the courtroom scene; it is the definition, an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a sudden seizure of power, an uprising or revolt.

clue.text: Defeat of Polish: not good

indicators.note: the letter for the next word is left out

parts.note: gloss is a polish or shine

explanation.surface: The Polish team's defeat was not a good one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the shine.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss is a defeat in a game or contest.

clue.text: Motoring group tours stop in Eastern part of France

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second as a tourist travels round

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
to quit is to stop
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A motoring club's tour pauses in an eastern French region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tours' looks like the French city, but it means going round: the motoring club's letters go round the word for stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquitaine is a region of south-western France.

clue.text: Not threatened with fine for criminal activity

parts.note: safe means free from danger
cracking is British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Being unthreatened and fined for a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Safecracking is breaking open safes to steal from them, a crime.

clue.text: Passing round valuable piece

parts.note: O is round in shape
the king is the most valuable chess piece

explanation.surface: Passing round a precious item.
explanation.definitionFit: OKing something is approving it, giving it a pass.

clue.text: Passenger back from the Orient

parts.note: a fare is a paying passenger in a taxi
astern means at or towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A traveller returns from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Far Eastern describes East Asia, the region once called the Orient.

clue.text: Disdainful comment on industrial action to shock

definitions.meaning: a sneer that a walkout is foolish
to leave someone speechless with astonishment

explanation.definitionFit: To strike someone dumb is to astonish them into silence; read as two words it scorns a strike.

clue.text: Celebratory turns as precursor to whisky and variable bread

parts.note: Victor comes just before Whisky in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Y is a letter used for a variable in algebra
rolls are small loaves of bread

explanation.surface: Turns made in triumph before whisky and assorted bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whisky' looks like the drink but is the NATO alphabet's W, preceded by Victor.
explanation.definitionFit: Victory rolls are aerobatic turns made by a pilot returning in triumph.

clue.text: Sort of erotic dancing establishment with which journalist specifically connected

parts.note: lap dancing is a kind of erotic dancing
a joint is slang for a bar or club
ED for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is linked with a strip club.
explanation.definitionFit: Lap-jointed describes timber joined by overlapping, a particular way of connecting.

clue.text: Boor reacts after upsetting language

indicators.note: upsetting the letters jumbles them

explanation.surface: A lout responds after being offended by some words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' reads as offending but rearranges BOOR REACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbo-Croat is the South Slavic language of Serbia, Croatia and neighbours.

clue.text: Waves welcoming left-winger following a substitute on pitch?

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first
one piece takes in the other

parts.note: surf is breaking waves
Trot is short for Trotskyist

explanation.surface: Waves embrace a leftist after a replacement comes onto the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' puts the leftist inside the waves, and 'following' sets all of that after A. 'pitch' is a sports field, not a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: AstroTurf is artificial grass used instead of turf on sports pitches.

clue.text: Kierkegaard maybe captivating university fellow

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: the philosopher Kierkegaard was a Dane

explanation.surface: The Danish philosopher charms an academic fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'university fellow' looks like an academic; 'fellow' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Duane is a man's first name, and a fellow is a man.

clue.text: German flower's scent picked up

indicators.note: heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a scent is an odour

explanation.surface: A German bloom's fragrance is noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a thing that flows, a river: the Oder runs along the German-Polish border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river forming part of Germany's border with Poland.

clue.text: Plan to emit loud blast

indicators.note: to give out, so the letter leaves the word

parts.note: a draft is a preliminary plan
F is forte, loud in music

explanation.surface: A scheme to give off a loud noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loud blast' looks like one phrase; 'loud' gives F and 'blast' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Drat is a mild curse, like the exclamation blast.
